seed.name: First Light
seed.blurb: The observatory’s opening picture, kept for good.

record.line: The observatory’s opening picture, kept for good.

seed.name: Imilac
seed.blurb: A pallasite: metal and crystal from deep inside an asteroid.

record.line: A pallasite: metal and crystal from deep inside an asteroid.

seed.name: Moon Rock
seed.blurb: Found in a desert, matched to Apollo samples by its chemistry.

record.line: Found in a desert, matched to Apollo samples by its chemistry.

seed.name: Earth
seed.blurb: Taken on Valentine’s Day 1990, looking back.

record.line: Taken on Valentine’s Day 1990, looking back.
story: Seven parts in ten of its surface are ocean.
The only world known to hold life.

seed.name: Earthrise
seed.blurb: Often called the picture that started the environmental movement.

record.line: Often called the picture that started the environmental movement.
story: Apollo 8 was the first crewed flight to the Moon.
Its crew read from Genesis on live television.

seed.name: The Dinosaur Asteroid
seed.blurb: Its crater, 180 km wide, lies buried under the Yucatán.

record.line: Its crater, 180 km wide, lies buried under the Yucatán.
story: It struck at about 20 km a second.
Soot and dust darkened the sky for years.

seed.name: The Tunguska Blast
seed.blurb: June 1908: its pressure wave was recorded in England.

record.line: June 1908: its pressure wave was recorded in England.
story: Its blast was hundreds of times stronger than Hiroshima.
The first expedition reached the site 19 years later.

seed.name: Sputnik 1
seed.blurb: It burned up three months later; the race it started did not.

record.line: It burned up three months later; the race it started did not.
story: A polished ball 58 cm across, with four long antennas.
It weighed about 84 kilograms.

seed.name: The Space Station
seed.blurb: Big as a football pitch, built by five space agencies.

record.line: Big as a football pitch, built by five space agencies.
story: It travels at about 28,000 km an hour.
On a clear dusk it outshines every star.

seed.name: The Hubble Space Telescope
seed.blurb: It helped measure the age of everything: 13.8 billion years.

record.line: It helped measure the age of everything: 13.8 billion years.
story: It circles the Earth about every 95 minutes.
Many of the pictures on the backs of these cards are its own.

seed.name: The James Webb Space Telescope
seed.blurb: It works 1.5 million km away, colder than −230 °C.

record.line: It works 1.5 million km away, colder than −230 °C.
story: Its sunshield is the size of a tennis court.
It folded like origami to fit inside its rocket.

seed.name: The Moon
seed.blurb: Its pull raises the tides in every ocean.

record.line: Its pull raises the tides in every ocean.
story: It is about a quarter as wide as the Earth.
Twelve people have walked on it.

seed.name: Apollo 11
seed.blurb: Collins circled alone above while they walked.

record.line: Collins circled alone above while they walked.
story: Eight days from launch to splashdown.
They brought back 21.5 kg of Moon rock.

seed.name: Tycho
seed.blurb: Surveyor 7 landed beside its rim in 1968.

record.line: Surveyor 7 landed beside its rim in 1968.

seed.name: The Sun
seed.blurb: Its light took tens of thousands of years to climb out of the core.

record.line: Its light took tens of thousands of years to climb out of the core.
story: It holds more than 99 percent of the Solar System’s mass.
Everything that lives is running on it.

seed.name: Mercury
seed.blurb: Ice hides in polar craters that sunlight never reaches.

record.line: Ice hides in polar craters that sunlight never reaches.
story: It has almost no air to hold the heat.
It never strays far from dusk or dawn.

seed.name: Venus
seed.blurb: It spins backwards: there the Sun rises in the west.

record.line: It spins backwards: there the Sun rises in the west.
story: Its air presses down ninety times harder than ours.
After the Moon, the brightest thing in the night.

seed.name: Mars
seed.blurb: Two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, circle it.

record.line: Two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, circle it.
story: Its red is rust in the dust.
A year there lasts 687 days.

seed.name: Olympus Mons
seed.blurb: Its slopes are so gentle you could walk to the top.

record.line: Its slopes are so gentle you could walk to the top.

seed.name: Valles Marineris
seed.blurb: Named for Mariner 9, the probe that found it in 1972.

record.line: Named for Mariner 9, the probe that found it in 1972.
story: Nearly ten times the length of the Grand Canyon.
Its walls show layers laid down over billions of years.

seed.name: Jupiter
seed.blurb: The largest planet, and the brightest of winter evenings.

record.line: The largest planet, and the brightest of winter evenings.

seed.name: Io
seed.blurb: It circles its planet in less than two days.

record.line: It circles its planet in less than two days.
story: Its lava runs hotter than any on Earth today.
Sulfur paints it yellow, orange and red.

seed.name: Europa
seed.blurb: A spacecraft called Clipper is on its way there.

record.line: A spacecraft called Clipper is on its way there.

seed.name: Ganymede
seed.blurb: Galileo spotted it in January 1610.

record.line: Galileo spotted it in January 1610.
story: Its grooves are faults in old, cracked ice.
The probe JUICE is on its way to orbit it.

seed.name: Comet Shoemaker–Levy 9
seed.blurb: Torn into pieces by a close pass two years before.

record.line: Torn into pieces by a close pass two years before.
story: Its pieces struck at about 60 km a second.
The dark marks on Jupiter lasted for months.

seed.name: The Rings of Saturn
seed.blurb: Its rings are wide as worlds, thin as a building.

record.line: Its rings are wide as worlds, thin as a building.

seed.name: Titan
seed.blurb: Huygens landed there in 2005, the farthest landing ever made.

record.line: Huygens landed there in 2005, the farthest landing ever made.
story: It is larger than the planet Mercury.
Sunlight there is about a hundredth of ours.

seed.name: Enceladus
seed.blurb: Its spray feeds one of Saturn’s rings.

record.line: Its spray feeds one of Saturn’s rings.
story: Cassini flew through its plumes and tasted salt.
Its south pole is warm, striped with long cracks.

seed.name: Uranus
seed.blurb: Herschel found it in 1781, the first planet found by telescope.

record.line: Herschel found it in 1781, the first planet found by telescope.
story: Its blue-green comes from methane in the air.
Thirteen faint rings circle it.

seed.name: Neptune
seed.blurb: Voyager 2 is the only craft to visit, in 1989.

record.line: Voyager 2 is the only craft to visit, in 1989.
story: Galle found it in 1846, within a degree of the prediction.
It has gone round the Sun once since it was found.

seed.name: Pluto
seed.blurb: Its discoverer’s ashes flew past it on New Horizons.

record.line: Its discoverer’s ashes flew past it on New Horizons.
story: Its biggest moon, Charon, is half its width.
It takes 248 of our years to go round the Sun.

seed.name: Halley
seed.blurb: Its logbook stays open until it returns.

record.line: Its logbook stays open until it returns.

seed.name: ʻOumuamua
seed.blurb: Its name is Hawaiian for a scout from far away.

record.line: Its name is Hawaiian for a scout from far away.
story: It sped up slightly as it left, and no one is sure why.
It is already beyond the orbit of Neptune.

seed.name: Voyager 1
seed.blurb: It carries a golden record of music and greetings.

record.line: It carries a golden record of music and greetings.

seed.name: The Big Dipper
seed.blurb: Five of its stars travel through space together.

record.line: Five of its stars travel through space together.
story: In some countries it is called the Plough.
Over thousands of years its shape slowly changes.

seed.name: Orion
seed.blurb: High on winter evenings, gone by summer.

record.line: High on winter evenings, gone by summer.
story: Its stars are hundreds of light-years apart, not neighbours.
Below the belt hangs a sword with a nebula in it.

seed.name: The Southern Cross
seed.blurb: Beside it lies the Coalsack, a dark cloud of dust.

record.line: Beside it lies the Coalsack, a dark cloud of dust.
story: Its long bar points toward the south pole of the sky.
Two bright pointers beside it lead the eye there.

seed.name: The Summer Triangle
seed.blurb: Deneb shines from 150 times farther away than Altair.

record.line: Deneb shines from 150 times farther away than Altair.
story: Altair spins once every nine hours.
Vega is the brightest of the three.

seed.name: Alpha Centauri
seed.blurb: Seen only from the south, the third-brightest star at night.

record.line: Seen only from the south, the third-brightest star at night.
story: Proxima is too faint to see without a telescope.
At our fastest probe’s speed, the trip would take millennia.

seed.name: Sirius
seed.blurb: Just 8.6 light-years away, one of our nearest neighbours.

record.line: Just 8.6 light-years away, one of our nearest neighbours.
story: It gives off about 25 times the Sun’s light.
Look for it low in winter, below Orion.

seed.name: Vega
seed.blurb: Blue-white and spinning so fast it bulges.

record.line: Blue-white and spinning so fast it bulges.
story: It is about 25 light-years away.
A disc of dust surrounds it.

seed.name: Arcturus
seed.blurb: Its light switched on the Chicago World’s Fair in 1933.

record.line: Its light switched on the Chicago World’s Fair in 1933.
story: The brightest star north of the celestial equator.
It is about 37 light-years away.

seed.name: Aldebaran
seed.blurb: The Moon often passes in front of it.

record.line: The Moon often passes in front of it.
story: About 44 times the width of the Sun.
Its name means “the follower” in Arabic.

seed.name: Polaris
seed.blurb: Really three stars, one of them a pulsing giant.

record.line: Really three stars, one of them a pulsing giant.
story: It sits less than a degree from the true pole.
It is about 430 light-years away.

seed.name: Mira
seed.blurb: It races through space at 130 km a second.

record.line: It races through space at 130 km a second.
story: It swells and shrinks over about eleven months.
One of the first stars seen to change in brightness.

seed.name: Betelgeuse
seed.blurb: About 550 light-years away, near the end of its life.

record.line: About 550 light-years away, near the end of its life.
story: Big telescopes can show it as a disc.
It is only about ten million years old.

seed.name: Antares
seed.blurb: Low in the south on summer evenings.

record.line: Low in the south on summer evenings.
story: It is about 550 light-years away.
It sits in the most colourful clouds in the sky.

seed.name: Rigel
seed.blurb: About 860 light-years away, only eight million years old.

record.line: About 860 light-years away, only eight million years old.
story: About 79 times the width of the Sun.
It is really a system of several stars.

seed.name: Eta Carinae
seed.blurb: 7,500 light-years away, and certain to explode one day.

record.line: 7,500 light-years away, and certain to explode one day.
story: It is really two massive stars in a tight orbit.
It cannot be seen from most of the north.

seed.name: TRAPPIST-1
seed.blurb: A year on the innermost planet lasts a day and a half.

record.line: A year on the innermost planet lasts a day and a half.
story: Its star is barely bigger than Jupiter.
It is about 40 light-years away.

seed.name: The Pleiades
seed.blurb: They drift through a dust cloud that is not their own.

record.line: They drift through a dust cloud that is not their own.

seed.name: The Beehive
seed.blurb: The Moon and planets often pass right through it.

record.line: The Moon and planets often pass right through it.
story: One of the nearest clusters to the Sun.
Its stars formed together, long before the Pleiades.

seed.name: The Helix
seed.blurb: About 650 light-years away, nearly as wide as the full Moon.

record.line: About 650 light-years away, nearly as wide as the full Moon.
story: Its glow is gas lit by the hot core left behind.
Within tens of thousands of years it will fade.

seed.name: The Ring Nebula
seed.blurb: Found in 1779, between two stars of the Lyre.

record.line: Found in 1779, between two stars of the Lyre.
story: It lies about 2,500 light-years away.
Even a small telescope shows its hollow centre.

seed.name: The Cat’s Eye
seed.blurb: Hubble’s 1994 picture of it stunned astronomers.

record.line: Hubble’s 1994 picture of it stunned astronomers.
story: It lies over 3,000 light-years away.
X-rays show hot gas at its heart.

seed.name: Orion Nebula
seed.blurb: Its glow covers more sky than the full Moon.

record.line: Its glow covers more sky than the full Moon.

seed.name: The Horsehead
seed.blurb: It will wear away in about five million years.

record.line: It will wear away in about five million years.
story: It is about 1,400 light-years away.
Behind it glows red hydrogen gas.

seed.name: The Rosette
seed.blurb: Look for it beside Orion, in the Unicorn.

record.line: Look for it beside Orion, in the Unicorn.
story: It lies about 5,000 light-years away.
Its hollow holds a cluster you can see in binoculars.

seed.name: The Veil
seed.blurb: Its brightest strand is called the Witch’s Broom.

record.line: Its brightest strand is called the Witch’s Broom.
story: It lies about 2,400 light-years away.
A filter makes its threads stand out in a small telescope.

seed.name: The Lagoon
seed.blurb: About 4,100 light-years away, toward the galaxy’s centre.

record.line: About 4,100 light-years away, toward the galaxy’s centre.
story: A young cluster sits inside it.
In the sky it spans about three full Moons.

seed.name: The Trifid
seed.blurb: Found by Messier in 1764.

record.line: Found by Messier in 1764.
story: It is about 4,000 light-years away.
New stars are still forming in its dark lanes.

seed.name: Pillars of Creation
seed.blurb: Hubble’s 1995 picture made them famous.

record.line: Hubble’s 1995 picture made them famous.
story: The pillars stand about 7,000 light-years away.
Webb saw them again in infrared in 2022.

seed.name: The Crab
seed.blurb: Lord Rosse named it in 1844, after his own drawing.

record.line: Lord Rosse named it in 1844, after his own drawing.

seed.name: The Carina Nebula
seed.blurb: Too far south to rise for most of Europe.

record.line: Too far south to rise for most of Europe.
story: It lies about 7,500 light-years away.
Eta Carinae, an unstable giant, sits inside it.

seed.name: Omega Centauri
seed.blurb: Halley saw it was a cluster, in 1677.

record.line: Halley saw it was a cluster, in 1677.
story: It is about 17,000 light-years away.
Its stars were born at different times, unlike most clusters.

seed.name: The Hercules Cluster
seed.blurb: Halley spotted it in 1714.

record.line: Halley spotted it in 1714.
story: Older than almost everything in the galaxy.
It lies over 20,000 light-years away.

seed.name: The Tarantula
seed.blurb: As close as Orion’s nebula, it would cast shadows.

record.line: As close as Orion’s nebula, it would cast shadows.
story: It is about 160,000 light-years away.
Supernova 1987A went off at its edge.

seed.name: The Milky Way
seed.blurb: A third of humanity can no longer see it at night.

record.line: A third of humanity can no longer see it at night.
story: It is about 100,000 light-years across.
At its centre sits a black hole of four million Suns.

seed.name: The Large Magellanic Cloud
seed.blurb: It is falling toward us, and will merge with us.

record.line: It is falling toward us, and will merge with us.
story: After our own, the brightest galaxy in the sky.
It holds the busiest star nursery near us.

seed.name: The Small Magellanic Cloud
seed.blurb: About 200,000 light-years away.

record.line: About 200,000 light-years away.
story: It holds a few hundred million stars.
It travels through space beside its bigger neighbour.

seed.name: Andromeda
seed.blurb: Its light set out 2.5 million years ago.

record.line: Its light set out 2.5 million years ago.

seed.name: The Triangulum
seed.blurb: About 2.7 million light-years away.

record.line: About 2.7 million light-years away.
story: The third-largest galaxy in our Local Group.
Its biggest nursery, NGC 604, is 1,500 light-years wide.

seed.name: The Cigar
seed.blurb: It shines five times brighter than the whole Milky Way.

record.line: It shines five times brighter than the whole Milky Way.
story: It lies about 12 million light-years away.
A supernova went off in it in 2014.

seed.name: Centaurus A
seed.blurb: About twelve million light-years away.

record.line: About twelve million light-years away.
story: The nearest giant elliptical galaxy to us.
From the south, binoculars show it as a soft glow.

seed.name: The Pinwheel
seed.blurb: About 21 million light-years away.

record.line: About 21 million light-years away.
story: It may hold a trillion stars.
It lies near the handle of the Big Dipper.

seed.name: The Whirlpool
seed.blurb: About 27 million light-years away, in the Hunting Dogs.

record.line: About 27 million light-years away, in the Hunting Dogs.
story: Lord Rosse drew its spiral in 1845.
Binoculars show it as a faint smudge.

seed.name: The Sombrero
seed.blurb: About 31 million light-years away, in Virgo.

record.line: About 31 million light-years away, in Virgo.
story: Its bulge is packed with old stars.
Its black ring is dust, where new stars form.

seed.name: M87
seed.blurb: Thousands of star clusters swarm around it.

record.line: Thousands of star clusters swarm around it.
story: The biggest galaxy near the heart of the Virgo cluster.
It is about 54 million light-years away.

seed.name: The Cartwheel
seed.blurb: 500 million light-years away, in the Sculptor.

record.line: 500 million light-years away, in the Sculptor.
story: Its ring is still spreading outward.
Webb photographed it in 2022.

seed.name: Sagittarius A*
seed.blurb: 26,000 light-years away, behind thick dust.

record.line: 26,000 light-years away, behind thick dust.

seed.name: Supernova 1987A
seed.blurb: It went off in a neighbour galaxy, the Large Magellanic Cloud.

record.line: It went off in a neighbour galaxy, the Large Magellanic Cloud.
story: First seen on 24 February 1987.
Its star was a blue supergiant, not a red one.

seed.name: TON 618
seed.blurb: About eleven billion light-years away, blazing as a quasar.

record.line: About eleven billion light-years away, blazing as a quasar.
story: One of the most massive black holes known.
It lies in the Hunting Dogs.

seed.name: The Deep Field
seed.blurb: Some of its galaxies are 12 billion years old.

record.line: Some of its galaxies are 12 billion years old.
story: The patch is smaller than a grain of sand at arm’s length.
It was taken in December 1995.

seed.name: The Oldest Light
seed.blurb: Found by accident in 1965 with a radio horn.

record.line: Found by accident in 1965 with a radio horn.
story: Released about 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
It fills the whole sky, in every direction.

seed.name: Total Solar Eclipse
seed.blurb: Somewhere on Earth, one comes every year or two.

record.line: Somewhere on Earth, one comes every year or two.
story: The Moon is 400 times smaller than the Sun, and 400 times nearer.
Totality never lasts more than about seven and a half minutes.

seed.name: Ring of Fire
seed.blurb: The light dims, but the day never turns to night.

record.line: The light dims, but the day never turns to night.
story: The Moon’s orbit is not a perfect circle.
Sunlight through leaves makes little rings on the ground.

seed.name: The Blood Moon
seed.blurb: The longest last nearly two hours.

record.line: The longest last nearly two hours.
story: It happens only at full Moon.
Dust in our air can make it darker.

seed.name: The Aurora
seed.blurb: Strong storms push it far from the poles.

record.line: Strong storms push it far from the poles.
story: The same lights glow around the south pole.
It also shines on Jupiter and Saturn.

seed.name: Transit of Venus
seed.blurb: They come in pairs, eight years apart.

record.line: They come in pairs, eight years apart.
story: Transits were once used to measure the distance to the Sun.
Only seven have ever been seen.

seed.name: Comet Hale–Bopp
seed.blurb: Its core is about 60 km wide, huge for a comet.

record.line: Its core is about 60 km wide, huge for a comet.
story: Two men found it on the same night in 1995.
It had two tails, one of dust and one of gas.

seed.name: The Leonid Storm
seed.blurb: Crumbs of Comet Tempel–Tuttle.

record.line: Crumbs of Comet Tempel–Tuttle.
story: They peak in mid-November each year.
The 1966 storm reached about forty a second.

seed.name: The Perseids
seed.blurb: They peak around 12 August, year after year.

record.line: They peak around 12 August, year after year.
story: The summer shower: warm nights and fast, bright meteors.
They seem to fly out of Perseus.

seed.name: Canyon Diablo
seed.blurb: The iron that dug Meteor Crater, 1.2 km across.

record.line: The iron that dug Meteor Crater, 1.2 km across.

seed.name: Gibeon
seed.blurb: Etched with acid, its metal shows crystals grown over millions of years.

record.line: Etched with acid, its metal shows crystals grown over millions of years.

seed.name: Campo del Cielo
seed.blurb: A shower of iron that left a field of craters in Argentina.

record.line: A shower of iron that left a field of craters in Argentina.

seed.name: Muonionalusta
seed.blurb: Among the oldest iron ever found, 4.565 billion years old.

record.line: Among the oldest iron ever found, 4.565 billion years old.

seed.name: Allende
seed.blurb: Its white flecks are the oldest solids in the Solar System.

record.line: Its white flecks are the oldest solids in the Solar System.

seed.name: The Orionids
seed.blurb: They seem to fly out of Orion’s club.

record.line: They seem to fly out of Orion’s club.

seed.name: Hunter’s Moon
seed.blurb: It follows the Harvest Moon, a month later.

record.line: It follows the Harvest Moon, a month later.

seed.name: The Moon Takes the Pleiades
seed.blurb: The Moon has no air, so each star goes out at once.

record.line: The Moon has no air, so each star goes out at once.

seed.name: The Geminids
seed.blurb: Their parent is 3200 Phaethon, a rock that acts like a comet.

record.line: Their parent is 3200 Phaethon, a rock that acts like a comet.

seed.name: Christmas Eve Supermoon
seed.blurb: The tides run a little higher while it is near.

record.line: The tides run a little higher while it is near.

seed.name: The Double Opposition
seed.blurb: Both rise at sunset and stay up all night.

record.line: Both rise at sunset and stay up all night.

seed.name: The Snow Moon Eclipse
seed.blurb: Named for the deepest month of winter.

record.line: Named for the deepest month of winter.

seed.name: The Great Eclipse
seed.blurb: Luxor gets the longest totality on land until 2114.

record.line: Luxor gets the longest totality on land until 2114.

seed.name: Phobos
seed.blurb: It circles Mars three times in a single Martian day.

record.line: It circles Mars three times in a single Martian day.
story: Its name is Greek for fear; its sister Deimos is dread.
It falls a little closer every century, and one day it will break apart.

seed.name: The Roadster
seed.blurb: Ten thrusters of compressed air, and a car that can leave the road.

record.line: Ten thrusters of compressed air, and a car that can leave the road.
story: At its reveal it vaulted over five cars on its own thrust.
The first ones are to be built in 2028.
